recent_open_items.title: This closes #2449, correct blank cell comparisons
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## Description

Blank cells were converted to numeric zero before every comparison. For a blank A1, this made `A1=""` return FALSE and `A1="0"` return TRUE.

Use an empty string when comparing a blank cell with text, FALSE when comparing it with a logical value, and zero otherwise. The change applies to all six comparison operators in either operand order.

## Related Issue

Fixes #2449.

## How Has This Been Tested

- The new regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Tests cover text, numbers, logical values, cell references, IF, error handling, arithmetic, and text joining.
- `go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 20m`
- `go test -race ./... -run '^TestCalc' -count=1 -timeout 10m`
- `go vet ./...`

Tested with Go 1.27.1 on macOS arm64.

A full race-enabled run was also attempted, but the process was killed before completion.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix

recent_open_items.title: This closes #2450, fix incorrect result of the binary search in lookup functions
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
# PR Details

## Description

Three changes in `lookupBinarySearch`, the path taken by HLOOKUP and VLOOKUP with `range_lookup` TRUE and by XLOOKUP with `search_mode` 2 or -2.

`lookupSkipBlank` moves the probe position off a blank cell to the nearest cell holding a value inside the still open interval, and ends the search when the interval holds only blanks. A blank used to be compared as the number 0 through `ToNumber()` and steered the search into the wrong half.

`lookupCompare` maps the `criteriaNe` that `compareFormulaArg` returns for a type mismatch onto the lookup sort order, in which all numbers come before all text. A text entry behind the numbers no longer aborts a numeric search.

The fallback to the nearest smaller match is now skipped for `matchModeExact` and `matchModeWildcard`, so an exact match mode returns no result instead of a neighbour.

recent_open_items.title: This closes #2448, fix incorrect equality result for a number and text operand
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
# PR Details

## Description

Adds the helper `numberTextMismatch` and calls it from `calcEq` and `calcNEq`. When one operand is a number and the other one is text, `=` returns FALSE and `<>` returns TRUE instead of falling through to the comparison of the formatted values.

The helper is declared above `calcEq` and reads only `Type` and the logical flag. It is called after the existing text against text branch, so `strings.EqualFold` keeps handling that case and `"a"="A"` stays TRUE. A logical value is excluded, it reaches the comparison as a number holding the logical flag and its behaviour is unchanged.

## Related Issue

Closes #2448

## Motivation and Context

`rOpd.Value() == lOpd.Value()` cannot tell the number 1 from the text "1", because both format to `1`. Excel 365 (Excel for the web, 16.0300) returns FALSE for `1="1"` and TRUE for `1<>"1"`. The ordering operators `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` already have the type branches for this; only `=` and `<>` were missing them.

recent_open_items.title: Honor strings_to_formulas for brace-wrapped array formulas
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Fixes #1212.

When `strings_to_formulas=False`, `write()` preserves `=1+2` as text but still converts `{=1+2}` into an array formula. Put both automatic formula branches under the existing option in `_write_token_as_string`. Explicit `write_formula()` and `write_array_formula()` calls continue to write formulas.

The regression tests inspect completed XLSX files from `write`, `write_row` and `write_column`, covering the default, enabled and disabled option in both normal and constant-memory modes. They also check explicit formula and string methods. The two disabled-option subcases fail before the fix.

Validation: 1782 unittest tests pass on Python 3.12 and 3.14; `make test_flake8` passes. Changed-file formatting and Pylint checks pass. `make lint` stops at 349 Ruff findings that are identical on the original and modified source; the full lint target is therefore not green locally. Excel/LibreOffice execution was not tested.

AI assistance: investigated, implemented and tested with Op

recent_open_items.title: Bug: strings_to_formulas=False still converts brace-wrapped strings to array formulas
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
### Current behavior

With XlsxWriter 3.2.9, `strings_to_formulas=False` leaves `=1+2` as text, but `{=1+2}` is still serialized as an array formula. This affects exports that need to preserve literal text.

The sample prints:
```text
A2 {'t': 'array', 'ref': 'A2'} 1+2
```

### Expected behavior

Should this option also disable automatic conversion of brace-wrapped array formulas? I would expect both strings to remain text when it is false, without changing the default or explicit formula-writing methods.

### Sample code to reproduce

```markdown
import io
import zipfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import xlsxwriter

output = io.BytesIO()
with xlsxwriter.Workbook(output, {"strings_to_formulas": False}) as workbook:
    worksheet = workbook.add_worksheet()
    worksheet.write("A1", "=1+2")
    worksheet.write("A2", "{=1+2}")
    worksheet.write_string("A3", "{=1+2}")

with zipfile.ZipFile(output) as archive:
    root = ET.fromstring(archive.read("xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml"))

recent_open_items.title: Speed up object positioning on uniform-height sheets
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Closes #1210.

This skips the repeated walk through earlier rows when a sheet only has a custom default row height.

All rows have the same height in that case, so the vertical offset can be worked out directly. If any row has its own settings, the method keeps the existing loop. The column calculations, offsets and remaining object-sizing steps are unchanged.

I kept `range()` in the short calculation so non-integer row indexes still raise the same errors and negative indexes keep the earlier empty-range offset.

For M objects across R rows, this removes up to O(M × R) earlier-row work and replaces it with O(M) on uniform-height sheets. It doesn't change the rest of workbook generation, and it doesn't add a cache or index. Extra working memory stays O(1).

### Checks

- 1,798 tests and 16 subtests passed, including 11 new regression tests.
- The original 1,787-test suite also passed with the pinned base method.
- 1,050 geometry comparisons and 22 extra output/error comparisons matched

recent_open_items.title: SVGImageRenderer: only load embedded resources from SVG pictures
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Repro: put an SVG picture in a .pptx whose markup contains `<image xlink:href="file:///path/to/secret.png" width="100" height="100"/>` or `<use xlink:href="file:///path/to/other.svg#id"/>`, then render the slide with `XSLFSlide.draw` or `PPTX2PNG`. The file is read from the local disk of the machine doing the rendering and drawn into the output, so a presentation converted to thumbnails on a server shows that server's images and SVG files in the result. `http:` references are already refused.
Cause: `SVGUserAgent` inherits `UserAgentAdapter.getExternalResourceSecurity`, which returns Batik's `DefaultExternalResourceSecurity` (a same-host check). `SVGImageRenderer` loads the picture with an empty document URI, so the document host is null, and a `file:` URL's host is null too, so the check passes.
Fix: `SVGUserAgent` returns `EmbededExternalResourceSecurity`, which allows only `data:` URLs. An SVG picture is self-contained in the package and has no location of its own to resolve against

recent_open_items.title: WorkbookEvaluator: walk a cell's consumers on invalidation without copying the set
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Item 5 of the evaluator performance list. **Measured effect is marginal — see the numbers before deciding whether it earns its place.**

### What it does

`CellCacheEntry.recurseClearCachedFormulaResults` (the walk behind `notifyUpdateCell`) called `getConsumingCells()` at every node, copying the consumer set to an array, because each consumer's `clearFormulaEntry()` removes it from the set being iterated. The walk now drains the set instead: `FormulaCellCacheEntrySet.peekAny()` returns some entry, clearing it removes it, repeat until the set is empty. A scan cursor carries on from where the last entry was found, so draining stays linear despite the holes removals leave in the open-addressing array (and survives the shrink re-hash). `containsPeeked` is an O(1) guard that turns a broken invariant (a consumer that does not list this cell as an input) into an `IllegalStateException` instead of an endless loop.
